title: Gender and Plural Suffixes
subtitle: Mastering masculine and feminine noun and adjective agreement
keyPoint: Hebrew nouns are either masculine or feminine, generally taking ים- for masculine plurals and ות- for feminine plurals, with modifying adjectives matching in both gender and number.

mistakes.note: Adjectives must match feminine singular nouns with the feminine ending.
Even if an irregular noun looks unusual, feminine nouns like אישה/נשים require feminine adjectives.
שולחן is grammatically masculine despite taking ות- in plural; adjectives match true grammatical gender.

quiz.question: Choose the correct phrase for 'big houses' (בית is masculine):
quiz.explanation: Although בית forms the irregular plural בתים with the standard masculine ending, its adjective must always be masculine plural (גדולים).

quiz.question: Select the correct phrase for 'new female students':
quiz.explanation: Both the feminine plural noun (תלמידות) and its adjective must take the feminine plural ending ות-.

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly says 'The chairs are comfortable' (כיסא is masculine):
quiz.explanation: כיסא takes an irregular plural ending (כיסאות), but remains masculine, so the adjective must be masculine plural (נוחים).

quiz.question: Choose the correct adjective form for 'חולצה' (shirt, feminine):
quiz.explanation: חולצה is a feminine singular noun, so it requires the feminine singular adjective לבנה.

tip: Always learn the gender of a noun in the singular; irregular plural endings like שולחנות (masculine) or מילים (feminine) never change the noun's true gender for adjective agreement.

title: The Definite Article (ה׳ הידיעה)
subtitle: Prefixing ha- to nouns and maintaining modifier agreement
keyPoint: The prefix ה- (ha-) marks a noun as definite, and unlike English, any adjective modifying that noun must also take the prefix ה-.

mistakes.note: To say 'the good book', both noun and adjective must take ה-. 'הספר טוב' means 'The book IS good'.
You cannot attach the definite article only to the adjective; the noun must have it as well.
The definite article ה- must be attached directly as a prefix to the word with no space.

quiz.question: How do you say 'the big dog' in Hebrew?
quiz.explanation: In an attributive definite phrase, both the noun and the adjective require the definite prefix: הכלב הגדול.

quiz.question: What does the sentence 'הקפה חם' mean?
quiz.explanation: Because חם lacks the prefix ה-, this forms a complete sentence: 'The coffee is hot'.

quiz.question: Complete the phrase 'the new apartment': הדירה ___
quiz.explanation: Since דירה is feminine singular and has the definite article ה-, the adjective must match: feminine singular with ה- (החדשה).

quiz.question: Which of the following phrases correctly translates 'the small cities' (ערים is feminine plural)?
quiz.explanation: ערים is feminine plural and definite, so the adjective must be feminine plural and definite: הערים הקטנות.

tip: Double check double ה-: If your English phrase is 'the [adjective] [noun]', Hebrew requires 'ha-[noun] ha-[adjective]'. Dropping the second ה turns it into a full sentence with 'is'!

title: The Direct Object Marker (את)
subtitle: Connecting transitive verbs to specific direct objects
keyPoint: The particle את (et) must be placed before a definite direct object (proper names, nouns with ה-, or possessives), but is completely omitted before indefinite nouns.

useCases.label: Definite Noun with Article
useCases.example: הם שותים את המיץ בארוחת הבוקר.

useCases.label: Person or City Name
useCases.example: אני מבקר את ירושלים ואת משה.

useCases.label: Indefinite Contrast
useCases.example: יוסי קונה ספר ולא את העיתון.

mistakes.right: אני אוהב שוקולד / אני אוהב את השוקולד
mistakes.note: Never use את before general or indefinite nouns that lack ה- or a definite identifier.
When the direct object is definite (הילד), את is mandatory and cannot be omitted.
את only marks direct objects received by transitive verbs, not destinations or directions.

quiz.question: Fill in the blank: 'אני רואה ___ מורה בכיתה.' (I see the teacher)
quiz.explanation: 'The teacher' is a definite direct object, requiring both the marker את and the article ה-.

quiz.question: Choose the correct translation for 'Ron drinks water':
quiz.explanation: 'Water' is indefinite in this sentence, so את must not be used.

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly says 'We know Michal'?
quiz.explanation: Proper names are inherently definite, so proper direct objects require את (without ה-).

quiz.question: Choose the correct translation: 'The girl is reading the letter.'
quiz.explanation: Because 'the letter' (המכתב) is definite, the transitive verb קוראת must take את המכתב.

tip: Think of את as an untranslatable grammatical flag: if you can point to a specific 'the' or a named person receiving the action, raise the 'את' flag!

title: Inseparable Prepositions (ב, ל, כ, מ)
subtitle: Attaching single-letter prepositions and merging definite articles
keyPoint: The single-letter prepositions ב- (in/at), ל- (to/for), כ- (as/like), and מ- (from) attach directly to nouns, and when combined with the definite article, ב/ל/כ absorb the ה and adopt its 'a' vowel.

cells: in a house / in the house
to a boy / to the boy
from a house / from the house
like a king / like the king

examples.en: דוד גר בבית גדול ליד הים.

mistakes.note: Prepositions cannot stand detached with spaces, and going 'to' requires ל-, not ב-.
When attaching ל-, ב-, or כ- to a definite noun, the letter ה drops and transfers its vowel (lah-khanut, not le-ha-khanut).
With מ-, the letter ה is NOT swallowed; it stays as מה- (me-ha-).

quiz.question: How do you write 'in the room' (the room = החדר) in Hebrew script?
quiz.explanation: When ב- attaches to a definite noun like החדר, the ה drops in spelling/speech (vowel becomes 'ba'), written simply as בחדר.

quiz.question: Which prefix correctly expresses 'from' in 'from the store'?
quiz.explanation: The preposition מ- keeps the definite article intact, prefixing as מה- (from the).

quiz.question: Fill in the blank: 'אנחנו נוסעים ___ תל אביב.' (to Tel Aviv)
quiz.explanation: Destination 'to' is denoted by the inseparable preposition ל- attached directly to תל אביב.

quiz.question: Choose the correct phrase for 'to a friend' (indefinite friend = חבר):
quiz.explanation: The preposition ל- prefixes directly to the indefinite noun without spaces: לחבר (le-khaver).

tip: Remember the acronym בֶּלֶ״ך (Be, Le, Ke): these three swallow the letter ה when definite (be + ha = ba, le + ha = la), while מ (Me) keeps the ה visible (me-ha-)!

title: Nominal Sentences and Existence (יש / אין)
subtitle: Forming present-tense equational sentences and expressing existence or possession
keyPoint: Hebrew has no present tense 'to be' (am/is/are), using direct noun-adjective placement instead, while existence and possession are expressed with יש (there is / to have) and אין (there is not / to not have).

mistakes.note: Do not attempt to insert a copula like 'is' or 'am'; simply juxtapose the subject and predicate.
Possession in Hebrew uses 'יש ל-' (there is to me), so adding unnecessary subject pronouns is ungrammatical.
Never negate יש with 'לא יש'; the negative existential word is strictly אין.

quiz.question: How do you say 'We do not have bread' in Hebrew?
quiz.explanation: Possession is negated using אין combined with the preposition ל- inflected for 'us' (לנו): אין לנו לחם.

quiz.question: Complete the equational sentence: 'היא ___' (She is a doctor [f.]):
quiz.explanation: In present-tense nominal sentences, the pronoun and noun link directly without any helper verb: היא רופאה.

quiz.question: Choose the Hebrew sentence meaning 'Is there water here?':
quiz.explanation: Existential 'is there' is expressed using יש: יש מים פה?

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly says 'I have a dog'?
quiz.explanation: Hebrew expresses 'I have' literally as 'there is to me': יש לי.

tip: To master possession in Hebrew, replace the English verb 'to have' in your mind with 'there is to...': 'יש לי' (there is to me), 'יש לך' (there is to you).

title: Binyan Pa'al Present Tense (Kotev Pattern)
subtitle: Conjugate foundational active verbs across masculine, feminine, singular, and plural
keyPoint: In Hebrew present tense, verbs do not conjugate by person (I, you, he), but only by the gender and number of the subject using four standard endings.

mistakes.wrong: אני כותב מכתב (spoken by a female speaker)
mistakes.note: The pronoun אני takes the feminine verb ending when the speaker is a woman.
Plural subjects require the plural verb suffix -im (-ים) or -ot (-ות).
Singular feminine subjects take the -et (-ת) pattern in Binyan Pa'al.

quiz.question: Sarah says: 'I am reading a book.' Which form fits? 'אני ___ ספר.'
quiz.explanation: Sarah is a feminine singular speaker, requiring the feminine singular present form קוראת.

quiz.question: Choose the correct form for 'The boys are learning Hebrew': 'הבנים ___ עברית.'
quiz.explanation: הבנים is masculine plural, requiring the plural suffix -im in לומדים.

quiz.question: Choose the masculine singular form: 'David ___ coffee now.' 'דוד ___ קפה עכשיו.'
quiz.explanation: David is masculine singular, so the root ש-ת-ה takes the masculine singular present form שותה.

quiz.question: Choose the correct form for 'The female students write well': 'הסטודנטיות ___ טוב.'
quiz.explanation: הסטודנטיות is feminine plural, demanding the feminine plural ending כותבות.

tip: Because Hebrew has no auxiliary verb like 'is/are' in the present tense, כותב means both 'writes' and 'is writing'.

title: Inflected Prepositions with Pronominal Suffixes
subtitle: Attach personal endings to prepositions like le-, be-, ot-, and al-
keyPoint: Hebrew combines prepositions directly with personal pronouns into single fused words instead of keeping them separate.

useCases.label: Topics of Thought or Speech with על

mistakes.note: Never place an independent pronoun like אני after an uninflected particle; fuse them into לי.
The direct object marker את inflects into אותו, אותה, etc., rather than taking raw pronouns.
The preposition על fuses using plural-type suffixes, yielding עליו, not על הוא.

quiz.question: Fill in the blank for 'I saw him yesterday': 'ראיתי ___ אתמול.'
quiz.explanation: אותו represents 'him' (direct object marker את + 3rd person singular masculine suffix).

quiz.question: Complete the phrase 'Do you (m.sg.) have time?': 'יש ___ זמן?'
quiz.explanation: לךָ (spelled לך) is the 2nd person masculine singular inflection of לְ־.

quiz.question: Complete 'She told us the news': 'היא אמרה ___ את החדשות.'
quiz.explanation: לנו means 'to us' (1st person plural).

quiz.question: Fill in 'Why are you talking about her?': 'למה אתם מדברים ___?'
quiz.explanation: עליה means 'about her' (preposition על inflected for 3rd person feminine singular).

tip: Prepositions fall into two suffix families: singular-style like לִי / בּוֹ and plural-style like עָלַי / אֵלָיו.

title: The Construct State (Smikhut)
subtitle: Link two nouns into compound phrases and definite chains
keyPoint: In a smikhut construct chain, only the final noun can take the definite article הַ־, which makes the entire chain definite.

useCases.label: Compounds & Fixed Terms
useCases.example: הילדים הולכים אל בית ספר ברגל.

examples.en: זה בית הספר הכי ישן בעיר.

mistakes.note: Never put the definite article ה- on the first word of a construct chain; attach it solely to the second noun.
Singular feminine nouns ending in ה- change to ת- when in the construct state (עוגה becomes עוגת).
Masculine plural nouns drop the final ם- and change ending to י- (ספרים becomes ספרי).

quiz.question: Which phrase correctly says 'the train station'?
quiz.explanation: In smikhut, the first noun drops its independent ending (תחנה -> תחנת) and the definite article ה- attaches only to the second noun.

quiz.question: Choose the correct construct form of 'עוגה' (cake) in 'lemon cake': '___ לימון.'
quiz.explanation: Feminine singular nouns ending in ה- systematically replace ה with ת in smikhut, giving עוגת.

quiz.question: How do you say 'the language teachers' (masculine plural)?
quiz.explanation: Plural construct drops the final mem (מורים -> מורי) and definiteness attaches to the second noun (השפה).

quiz.question: Which of the following represents a correct indefinite smikhut for 'orange juice'?
quiz.explanation: מיץ תפוזים is the standard indefinite construct pair for 'orange juice' without any definite articles.

tip: Adjectives modifying a smikhut phrase always appear at the very end of the entire chain and match the gender and number of the FIRST noun.

title: Binyan Pa'al Past Tense Conjugation
subtitle: Conjugate three-letter roots using person-identifying suffixes
keyPoint: Unlike the present tense, Hebrew past tense verbs conjugate across all grammatical persons by appending distinct person-identifying suffixes to the base stem.

useCases.label: Completed Past Actions
useCases.example: אתמול שמרתי על הילדים של אחותי.

useCases.label: Narrating Sequential Events
useCases.example: הוא חזר הביתה, פתח את הדלת ואכל.

examples.en: איפה קנית את החולצה היפה הזאת?
הם סגרו את כל החלונות בגלל הגשם.
אנחנו פגשנו את דני במרכז העיר.

mistakes.note: Do not use present tense verbs for completed past actions; use the past tense form with -ti (-תי).
Learners often write an extra letter hey (כתבתה); the masculine 2nd-person suffix is spelled simply with a tav (כתבת).
The 3rd person plural past suffix is simply vav (־וּ), not an added mem.

quiz.question: Fill in the blank for 'I learned Hebrew yesterday': 'אתמול ___ עברית.'
quiz.explanation: The first-person singular past suffix is -ti (־תִּי), producing למדתי.

quiz.question: Fill in the blank for 'They closed the restaurant early': 'הם ___ את המסעדה מוקדם.'
quiz.explanation: The 3rd person plural past suffix for both masculine and feminine is -u (־וּ), giving סגרו.

quiz.question: Fill in the blank for 'We met a good friend': 'אנחנו ___ חבר טוב.'
quiz.explanation: The 1st person plural suffix is -nu (־נוּ), yielding פגשנו.

quiz.question: Which verb correctly completes 'She wrote an email': 'היא ___ מייל'?
quiz.explanation: 3rd person feminine singular takes a kamats + hey suffix (־ָה), yielding כָּתְבָה.

tip: The 3rd-person masculine singular form (כָּתַב) has no suffix; it is the dictionary citation root for past tense verbs.

title: Binyan Pi'el (Present and Past)
subtitle: Active intensive verbs marked by present prefix m- and characteristic vowels
keyPoint: In Binyan Pi'el, every present tense verb begins with the prefix מְ־, while the past tense features an 'i-e' vowel template.

examples.en: דני חיפש את המפתחות שלו שעה.

mistakes.wrong: אני דובר עברית. (meaning: I am speaking Hebrew right now)
mistakes.note: To express speaking as an active verb, use Binyan Pi'el (מדבר), not the Pa'al noun/participle דובר (which means 'spokesperson').
The root ד-ב-ר belongs to Binyan Pi'el; its past stem uses the 'i' vowel (דיברתי), never Pa'al vowels.
Feminine singular subjects require the feminine suffix -et (מדברת) in the present tense.

quiz.question: Which verb correctly fills 'She is speaking on the phone': 'היא ___ בטלפון'?
quiz.explanation: היא is feminine singular, requiring the Pi'el feminine present form מדברת.

quiz.question: Fill in the blank for 'I paid for the tickets': '___ על הכרטיסים.'
quiz.explanation: The 1st person singular past in Pi'el adds -ti to the stem (שִׁילַּמְתִּי).

quiz.question: Choose the past tense for 'He searched for his dog': 'הוא ___ את הכלב שלו.'
quiz.explanation: The 3rd person masculine singular past in Pi'el follows the 'i-e' stem pattern without suffix: חִיפֵּשׂ.

quiz.question: Choose the masculine plural present form for 'They are looking for an apartment': 'הם ___ דירה.'
quiz.explanation: Masculine plural in Pi'el takes the m- prefix plus the plural suffix -im (מְחַפְּשִׂים).

tip: Almost all verbs in Binyan Pi'el share the letter mem (מ) as their very first letter in the present tense.

title: Binyan Hif'il: The Causative Stem
subtitle: Forming causative and active verbs with characteristic prefixes
keyPoint: Binyan Hif'il typically conveys causative actions marked by a he- prefix in the past tense and a ma- prefix in the present tense.

mistakes.note: The root ס-ב-ר belongs to Hif'il for 'explaining', requiring the הִ- prefix in the past.
While pronoun inclusion isn't strictly ungrammatical, dropping redundant subject pronouns like אני in past 1st-person is natural; more critically, avoid confusing Hif'il suffixes with Pa'al.
Present tense verbs in Hif'il must agree in gender; feminine singular takes the ־ָה (-ah) ending.

quiz.question: Yesterday, Dan ___ pizza for everyone.
quiz.explanation: The past tense masculine singular in Binyan Hif'il uses the prefix הִ- (hizmin).

quiz.question: The teacher (f.sg) ___ the new words right now.
quiz.explanation: Present tense feminine singular uses the prefix מַ- with feminine suffix ־ָה (masbirah).

quiz.question: Do you want ___ to the radio?
quiz.explanation: After modal verbs like want, use the infinitive which in Hif'il starts with לְהַ- (lehaqshiv).

quiz.question: Tomorrow we ___ the new project.
quiz.explanation: Future tense 1st person plural (we) takes the prefix נַ- (natchil).

tip: Spot Hif'il easily in vocabulary lists: present tense verbs almost always open with 'ma-' or 'me-', while past tense forms open with 'hi-'.

title: Binyan Hitpa'el: Reflexive and Reciprocal
subtitle: Mastering the hit- prefix and sibilant letter shifts
keyPoint: Binyan Hitpa'el indicates reflexive or reciprocal actions using the prefix הִתְ- (hit-), which swaps positions when the root begins with a sibilant consonant like ש or ס.

mistakes.note: When the root starts with ש, the prefix letter ת must swap places with it (metathesis).
Roots starting with ס also swap positions with the prefix ת, yielding הִסְתַּ- instead of הִתְסַ-.
With root letter ז, the prefix ת swaps and also changes into a ד to harmonize voicing.

quiz.question: Noa ___ every morning before school.
quiz.explanation: Roots starting with ס undergo metathesis: the ת moves behind the ס, producing מִסְתָּרֶקֶת.

quiz.question: Yesterday they ___ outside the cinema.
quiz.explanation: Past tense 3rd person plural for 'saw each other' is הִתְרָאוּ (hitra'u).

quiz.question: I usually ___ by train to work.
quiz.explanation: מִשְׁתַּמֵּשׁ (uses) features metathesis between ש and ת and fits the context of using transport.

quiz.question: The boy ___ when his mother entered.
quiz.explanation: Past tense masculine singular of ב-ו-ש/ב-י-ש in Hitpa'el is הִתְבַּיֵּשׁ (was shy / ashamed).

tip: Whenever you encounter a root starting with ש, שׂ, ס, or צ in Hitpa'el, remember the 'dance step': the prefix ת always steps behind that first consonant!

title: Weak Roots in Pa'al: Gutturals and Hollow Verbs
subtitle: Navigating vowel shifts and disappearing middle letters
keyPoint: Hollow roots collapse their middle vav or yod in the past tense into a two-letter base, while guttural consonants force neighboring vowels to shift toward 'a' (patach).

useCases.label: Hollow Verbs (Movement/State)
useCases.example: הוּא קָם בְּשֶׁבַע בַּבֹּקֶר כָּל יוֹם.

useCases.label: Guttural Final Consonants (ח/ע)
useCases.example: אֲנִי שׁוֹמֵעַ אֶת הַמּוּזִיקָה הַיָּפָה הַזֹּאת.

useCases.label: Travel and Living Hollow Roots
useCases.example: הֵם גָּרִים בִּירוּשָׁלַיִם כְּבָר חָמֵשׁ שָׁנִים.

examples.en: הִיא שָׂמָה אֶת הַמַּפְתְּחוֹת עַל הַשֻּׁלְחָן.
הֵם לֹא יָדְעוּ מָה לַעֲשׂוֹת בַּמַּצָּב הַזֶּה.

mistakes.note: Hollow roots like ק-ו-ם lose their middle vav in past tense 3rd person; never conjugate them like standard three-letter strong roots.
Final gutturals (ח and ע) demand an 'a' glide (patach gnuvah) right before them, pronounced 'shome'a'.

mistakes.wrong: אֶתְמוֹל שַׁרְתִּי שִׁיר וְהוּא שָׁיַר אִתִּי.
mistakes.right: אֶתְמוֹל שַׁרְתִּי שִׁיר וְהוּא שָׁר אִתִּי.
mistakes.note: The middle yod of ש-י-ר drops out in 3rd person past, giving שָׁר rather than a tri-consonantal שָׁיַר.

quiz.question: Yesterday, Sarah ___ from Tel Aviv to London.
quiz.explanation: In hollow roots (ט-ו-ס), the past feminine singular is formed by adding ־ָה to the two-letter base: טָסָה (tasa).

quiz.question: I (m.sg) am ___ the window because it is hot.
quiz.explanation: Roots ending in guttural ח take a furtive patach in the present masculine singular: פּוֹתֵחַ (pote'ach).

quiz.question: We ___ in an apartment near the sea last year.
quiz.explanation: The past 1st-person plural of ג-ו-ר takes the two-letter stem plus standard suffix ־נוּ: גַּרְנוּ (garnu).

quiz.question: Dan ___ his coffee very fast this morning.
quiz.explanation: Weak Lamed-He root ש-ת-ה in past 3rd person masculine singular becomes שָׁתָה (shata).

tip: For hollow verbs (ק-ו-ם, ג-ו-ר, ש-ׂי-ם), the 3rd person masculine singular past (קָם) and present (קָם) look identical without vowel marks; context will clarify tense!

title: Future Tense Formation Across Binyanim
subtitle: Mastering the א-ת-י-נ prefix system and vowel variations
keyPoint: The future tense in Hebrew is formed by attaching the person prefixes א-ת-י-נ (E-Ti-Yi-Ni) to stem bases whose vowel patterns depend on the binyan.

useCases.label: Promises and Commitments
useCases.example: אֲנִי אֶתְקַשֵּׁר אֵלֶיךָ מִיָּד אַחֲרֵי הַפְּגִישָׁה.

examples.en: מָחָר אֲנִי אֶקְנֶה מַתָּנָה לְיוֹם הַהֻלֶּדֶת.
אַתְּ תִּמְצְאִי אֶת הַתְּשׁוּבָה בַּסֵּפֶר הַזֶּה.
אֲנַחְנוּ נְסַדֵּר אֶת הַחֶדֶר לִפְנֵי שֶׁהֵם יַגִּיעוּ.
הוּא יַסְבִּיר לָנוּ אֶת הַכְּלָלִים הַחֲדָשִׁים.

mistakes.note: First person singular ('I') takes the prefix אֶ- (Alef), never יִ- (Yod), which marks 3rd person 'he'.
First person plural ('we') always uses prefix נ- (Nun), not י- with plural suffix ־וּ.
The suffix ־ִי (-i) is strictly for 2nd person feminine singular ('you, f.'), not masculine.

quiz.question: Tomorrow, Miriam (she) ___ to her parents.
quiz.explanation: Third person feminine singular takes the prefix תִּ- (tichtov), identical in form to 2nd m.sg.

quiz.question: Next week, I ___ a new car.
quiz.explanation: First person singular ('I') always uses the Alef prefix: אֶקְנֶה (eqneh).

quiz.question: The children (they) ___ all afternoon in the yard.
quiz.explanation: Third person plural ('they') uses prefix י- and suffix ־וּ: יְשַׂחֲקוּ (yesachaku).

quiz.question: When ___ you (m.pl) arrive home tonight?
quiz.explanation: Second person plural ('you all') takes prefix תַּ- and suffix ־וּ: תַּגִּיעוּ (tagi'u).

tip: Remember the acronym אֵיתָ"ן (EITAN): א (I), י (he/they), ת (you/she), נ (we). It matches the four prefixes of Hebrew future tense!

title: Infinitives (Shem Ha-Po'al) and Verb Complements
subtitle: Deriving l-prefixed infinitives and pairing them with modal verbs
keyPoint: The Hebrew infinitive (שם הפועל) always begins with the prefix לְ- (le-) and combines with modal verbs like רוֹצֶה, יָכוֹל, and צָרִיךְ without needing a subordinator.

useCases.label: Ability with יָכוֹל (Can / Able)
useCases.example: אַתָּה יָכוֹל לַעֲזֹר לִי עִם הַשִּׂיחָה?

examples.en: הִיא לֹא יְכוֹלָה לָבוֹא לַמְּסִבָּה הָעֶרֶב.

mistakes.note: Do not insert שֶׁ- (that) before an infinitive; connect the modal directly to the לְ- verb.
Hebrew infinitives strictly require the prefix לְ- (le- / li-); you cannot use a bare root stem.
Avoid confusing לִלְמֹד (Pa'al: to learn) with לְלַמֵּד (Pi'el: to teach).

quiz.question: Can you (m.sg) ___ the doctor today?
quiz.explanation: After modal יָכוֹל (can), the infinitive construct form with prefix לְ- is required: לִרְאוֹת (to see).

quiz.question: It is forbidden ___ photos inside the museum.
quiz.explanation: Impersonal modal phrases like אָסוּר (forbidden) are directly followed by the Pi'el infinitive לְצַלֵּם.

quiz.question: We want ___ a table at the restaurant.
quiz.explanation: Hif'il infinitive takes the לְהַ- prefix: לְהַזְמִין (to order / invite).

quiz.question: You must ___ on the road while driving.
quiz.explanation: After צָרִיךְ (must/need), the Hitpa'el infinitive begins with לְהִתְ- (or לְהִסְתַּ- with metathesis).

tip: Every Hebrew infinitive starts with the letter לַ/לְ (Lamed). If your verb complement doesn't start with ל-, it isn't an infinitive!

title: Possessive Suffixes on Nouns
subtitle: Attach pronominal endings directly to singular and plural nouns
keyPoint: Direct possessive suffixes attach to the construct base of nouns, distinguishing singular from plural stems.

useCases.label: Plural Possessed Noun
useCases.example: הוא סידר את כל ספריו על המדף.

useCases.label: Kinship and Family Terms
useCases.example: אבי ואמי גרים בעיר הזאת שנים רבות.

examples.en: קראתי את ספרו החדש בעניין רב.
היא שוחחה עם מורתה על תוצאות המבחן.
כל חבריו הגיעו למסיבת יום ההולדת.
זהו ביתנו החדש ליד חוף הים.
הילדים מצאו את משחקיהם בחדר השני.

mistakes.note: Never add the definite article ה to a noun with a pronominal possessive suffix because the suffix already makes it definite.
Do not duplicate the possessor with both a bound suffix and separate pronoun unless intentional poetic emphasis is needed.
Ensure the plural stem matches the correct grammatical person instead of mixing third and first person markers.

quiz.question: Choose the correct Hebrew word for 'his book':
quiz.explanation: The suffix -o (ו) attaches to a singular stem to denote third-person masculine possession.

quiz.question: Choose the correct Hebrew word for 'his books' (plural possessed):
quiz.explanation: Plural nouns take -av (יו) for 'his', marked orthographically by yod-vav.

quiz.question: Complete the sentence: 'This is our house' -> 'זהו ___ החדש.'
quiz.explanation: The suffix -nu (נו) indicates first-person plural possession ('our').

quiz.question: Choose the correct form for 'her teacher' (female teacher possessed by her):
quiz.explanation: Nouns ending in feminine -ah change to construct -at- before suffixes, yielding moratah (מורתה).

tip: Look for the letter yod (י) before the final suffix letter: it almost always signals that the possessed noun is plural (e.g., ספרו vs ספריו).

title: The Subordinating Prefix She- and Resumptive Pronouns
subtitle: Connect relative clauses and handle required resumptive prepositions
keyPoint: The prefix ש- introduces relative clauses, requiring a resumptive prepositional pronoun when relativizing oblique objects.

useCases.label: Prepositional Object Resumption
useCases.example: זה הנושא שחשבתי עליו כל השבוע.

examples.en: זה האיש שעזר לי למצוא את הדרך.
האישה שדיברתי איתה היא רופאה מפורסמת.
הנושא שחשבנו עליו עלה שוב בישיבה.
הדירה שגרנו בה הייתה קטנה אך נעימה.
הספר שקראתי אתמול ריתק אותי לגמרי.

mistakes.note: Hebrew prepositions cannot dangle at the end of a clause; they must combine with a resumptive pronoun.
In standard Hebrew, use ש- with a resumptive pronoun (בו) rather than colloquial איפה ש-.
The complementizer ש- attaches directly to the following word with no space, and redundant subject pronouns are omitted.

quiz.question: Complete the sentence: 'The woman that I wrote to (her)' -> 'האישה שכתבתי ___.'
quiz.explanation: The feminine singular antecedent האישה requires the matching feminine prepositional pronoun אליה (to her).

quiz.question: Complete the relative clause: 'The problem that we spoke about (it)' -> 'הבעיה שדיברנו ___.'
quiz.explanation: The noun בעיה is feminine singular, so the resumptive pronoun after על must be עליה.

quiz.question: Which sentence correctly attaches the prefix ש-?
quiz.explanation: The prefix ש- is proclitic and attaches directly to the next word with no intervening space.

quiz.question: Complete the sentence: 'The city that we live in (it)' -> 'העיר שאנחנו גרים ___.'
quiz.explanation: The noun עיר is feminine singular, requiring the prepositional form בה (in it).

tip: Hebrew never strands prepositions. If an English sentence ends in 'about', 'with', or 'in', Hebrew attaches a pronoun to that preposition inside the relative clause.

title: Binyan Nif'al (Passive of Pa'al and Middle Voice)
subtitle: Conjugate N-prefix verbs in past, present, and assimilating future stems
keyPoint: Binyan Nif'al marks the passive or reflexive of Pa'al, displaying a prefixed נ- in past/present that assimilates into the first root letter in future forms.

useCases.label: Reciprocal or Middle Voice
useCases.example: הם נפגשו בבית הקפה לאחר שנים רבות.

examples.en: קשה מאוד להיכנס לבניין ללא אישור.
הפגישה נקבעה לשעה שלוש אחר הצהריים.

mistakes.note: In future tense Nif'al, the nun assimilates into the first root letter (marked by dagesh or double yod in unvocalized text).
The infinitive of Nif'al uses the prefix לה- (le-hi-), never ל- with a nun prefix.
Pa'al פתח is transitive; when the door opens intransitively/passively, use Nif'al נפתח.

quiz.question: Identify the past tense 3ms Nif'al form of the root כ-ת-ב:
quiz.explanation: נכתב is the standard past 3ms form of Nif'al (nikhtav).

quiz.question: What is the future 3ms form of Nif'al for the root ס-ג-ר ('it will be closed')?
quiz.explanation: In future Nif'al, the prefix takes i-vowel and the nun assimilates into the samekh, written ייסגר in ktiv male.

quiz.question: Choose the correct Nif'al infinitive form meaning 'to meet':
quiz.explanation: Nif'al infinitives take the template להיפעל (le-hipa'el), producing להיפגש.

quiz.question: Complete the sentence: 'The window was broken yesterday' -> 'החלון ___ אתמול.'
quiz.explanation: חלון is grammatically masculine, requiring the masculine singular past Nif'al verb נשבר.

tip: In unvocalized spelling (כתיב מלא), future Nif'al often appears with double yod (ייכנס, ייפתח) to reflect the assimilation of the historical nun.

title: Internal Passives (Binyanim Pu'al and Huf'al)
subtitle: Form and recognize the direct passive counterparts of Pi'el and Hif'il
keyPoint: Pu'al and Huf'al serve as the vowel-internal passives of Pi'el and Hif'il, featuring characteristic u/o vowels and lacking imperative or true independent infinitive forms.

examples.en: הפרויקט החדש בוטל עקב חוסר תקציב.
האיש מובהל כעת לבית החולים בניידת טיפול נמרץ.
הודעה רשמית תפורסם בעיתונות מחר בבוקר.

mistakes.note: Do not add the Hif'il prefix ה- to Pu'al verbs; Pu'al mirrors Pi'el stem shapes with u-a vowels.
Huf'al (הוזמן) is passive and cannot take a direct object with את; use active Hif'il (הזמין) for transitive action.
Pu'al has no productive infinitive of its own; Hebrew uses the reflexive/middle Hitpa'el infinitive instead.

quiz.question: Which of the following is the Pu'al passive of the Pi'el verb ביטל ('he cancelled')?
quiz.explanation: בוטל is the past 3ms Pu'al form corresponding directly to active ביטל.

quiz.question: Identify the Huf'al form meaning 'was invited / ordered':
quiz.explanation: הוזמן (huzman) is the past 3ms Huf'al form derived from root ז-מ-נ.

quiz.question: Complete the sentence: 'The bill was paid' -> 'החשבון ___.'
quiz.explanation: The passive of שילם (he paid) is the Pu'al form שולם (was paid).

quiz.question: What is the present participle (ms) of the Huf'al verb 'to be recommended' (root מ-ל-צ)?
quiz.explanation: Huf'al present participles take the prefix מ- with an u/o vowel (mumlatz = מומלץ).

tip: The vowel 'u' (spelled with vav ו in modern script) immediately after the first root letter in past tense strongly indicates Pu'al (סודר, שולם) or Huf'al (הוסבר, הוזמן).

title: Action Nouns (Shem Pe'ulah) and Root Derivation
subtitle: Derive systematic nominal forms from each binyan pattern
keyPoint: Every active binyan possesses a primary nominalized pattern (משקל) used to express the abstract action of the verb.

useCases.label: Hif'il Causative Nominalization
useCases.example: החלטת ההנהלה התקבלה לאחר דיון ארוך.

examples.en: ההסבר של המרצה היה ברור ומעמיק.
סיום הקורס ייחגג בטקס מיוחד בשבוע הבא.

mistakes.note: Action nouns ending in -ah (ה-) or -ut (ות-) are grammatically feminine and require feminine agreement.
למידה is feminine; ensure predicative adjectives and verbs agree in gender.
Do not use the construct form (סמיכות) ending in -at before the preposition של.

quiz.question: What is the standard action noun (shem pe'ulah) of the Pa'al verb שמר ('to guard/keep')?
quiz.explanation: Pa'al regularly derives feminine action nouns in the qətilah pattern: שמירה (shmirah).

quiz.question: Choose the Pi'el action noun derived from the verb לימד ('to teach'):
quiz.explanation: Pi'el derives action nouns in the qitul pattern: לימוד (limud), distinct from Pa'al למידה (lmidah).

quiz.question: What is the Hif'il action noun corresponding to the verb הזמין ('to invite / order')?
quiz.explanation: Hif'il forms action nouns on the haqtalah pattern, producing הזמנה (hazmanah).

quiz.question: Choose the Hitpa'el action noun derived from התפתח ('to develop'):
quiz.explanation: Hitpa'el forms feminine abstract action nouns ending in -ut: התפתחות (hitpatkhut).

tip: Pairs from the same root change nuance by binyan: root ל-מ-ד gives למידה (learning, Pa'al) versus לימוד (instruction/study, Pi'el).
